questions: What is the precise definition of "coprime positive integers" - does this mean gcd(P,Q)=1 or that P and Q share no common factors other than 1?
How should we handle the case when x is an integer - should we express it as x/1 or consider other representations?
Is the sequence S required to consist only of positive integers, or can it include zero or negative values?
What constitutes a "good sequence" when N=1 (since the constraint mentions i from 1 to N-1 which would be empty)?
Should we consider sequences with repeated elements, or must all elements of S be distinct?
How do we interpret f(x) when x=P/Q and either P or Q is not in lowest terms initially?
Are there any additional constraints on the values in sequence S beyond being positive integers?
What is the expected behavior when the input values A_i are such that no valid sequence S exists?
answers: gcd(P,Q)=1, the standard definition of coprime (equivalent to sharing no common factors other than 1).
If x is an integer, express it as x/1, giving Q=1.
Yes, S consists only of positive integers, as stated.
Not applicable; N is guaranteed to be at least 2 per the constraints.
Not specified beyond the given conditions; repeated elements aren't explicitly disallowed.
f(x) is always defined via P,Q already reduced to lowest terms (coprime) by definition.
Not specified beyond being positive integers satisfying the stated equations and gcd condition.
Not explicitly addressed; if no valid S satisfies the conditions, the sum over the empty set of good sequences is 0.
inline_prompts:
For a positive rational number x, define f(x) as follows:
Express x as $\dfrac{P}{Q}$ using coprime positive integers P and Q, where gcd(P,Q)=1, the standard definition of coprime (equivalent to sharing no common factors other than 1). f(x) is defined as the value P\times Q.
You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_{N-1}) of positive integers of length N-1.
We call a sequence S=(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N) of positive integers of length N a good sequence if it satisfies all of the following conditions:
- For every integer i with 1\leq i\leq N-1, it holds that f\left(\dfrac{S_i}{S_{i+1}}\right)=A_i.
- $\gcd(S_1,S_2,\dots,S_N)=1$.
Define the score of a sequence as the product of all its elements.
Find the sum, modulo 998244353, of the scores of all good sequences.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
A_1 A_2 \dots A_{N-1}
Output
Print the sum, modulo 998244353, of the scores of all good sequences.
Constraints
- 2\leq N\leq 1000
- 1\leq A_i\leq 1000 (1\leq i\leq N-1)
- All input values are integers.
